subject: Service principals & automated provisioning — evidence request and role ownership clarifications
messages:
From: Aisha Clarke <security@medsys.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: Jake Morales <jake.morales@medsys.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — service principals & automated provisioning

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our SIG/SOC2 intake we're trying to collect artifacts that demonstrate how Redwood handles non-interactive/service principals and automated onboarding flows. Specifically can you provide:

- A snapshot of service principals (service accounts) created in the last 12 months, including creation timestamp, provisioning source (SCIM / API / Console), and owner (email)
- Example SAML assertions that show audience/recipient for machine-to-machine assertions (redact token values)
- SCIM delta sample showing an automated provisioning event from a third-party IdP into Redwood
- Role ownership mapping for any roles that map to elevated service access (list of role -> owner)
- Notes on ephemeral credential rotation for service principals and any JIT patterns used

Can we get a delivery by EOD Wednesday Pacific? We will need files uploaded to the SFTP location listed on the HubSpot ticket. Also flag any items that contain PII — we will need redaction guidance.

Appreciate it — Aisha

Aisha Clarke
Sr. Information Security Manager, MedSys Health
security@medsys.com

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Aisha Clarke <security@medsys.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — service principals & automated provisioning

Thanks Aisha — got this. Quick confirmations and plan:  

1) Scope: We'll provide a scoped snapshot for the last 12 months and a redaction-friendly sample of SAML assertions and SCIM deltas. For privacy we will:
  - remove any user personal identifiers beyond owner email prefixes (we'll truncate domain where requested)
  - redact token/assertion values but preserve attributes and timestamps

2) Deliverables (tentative):
  - redwood-service-principals-snapshot-20260614.csv (columns: id, created_at, provision_source, owner_email, role_bindings)
  - scim-delta-sample-20260531.json (redacted event showing provisioning source + attributes)
  - role-owner-roster-202605.xlsx (role -> owner -> last_reviewed)
  - a short README.md explaining redaction and query used to extract artifacts

3) Questions: 
  - For SAML assertions, do you want a raw assertion (redacted) or only the parsed attribute map? Many auditors prefer the parsed map plus one redacted raw assertion for verification.
  - For owner email truncation — is it acceptable to provide the owner as first_initial + last_name@<redacted> or do you need full email addresses?

I'll assemble the snapshot and have PrIyom prepare the SCIM sample and role roster. We will upload to the SFTP path on Wed EOD as requested unless you need the SAML sample earlier.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Aisha Clarke <security@medsys.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — service principals & automated provisioning

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 11:05 AM nikhil_sharma@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks Aisha — got this. Quick confirmations and plan:
> 
> 1) Scope: We'll provide a scoped snapshot for the last 12 months and a redaction-friendly sample of SAML assertions and SCIM deltas.

Adding the extraction notes and attachments we're preparing:

- Attached: redwood-service-principals-snapshot-20260614.csv (CSV export from our identity index; owners are provided as email but we can truncate domain if requested)
- Attached: scim-delta-sample-20260531.json (single provisioning event from Okta -> Redwood; contains attributes: externalId, displayName, groups)
- Attached: role-owner-roster-202605.xlsx (hand-curated by product access team; last_reviewed column reflects ownership confirmations from May 2026)

Rotation/JIT notes (short):
- We rotate ephemeral service tokens every 7 days via an internal token service; long-lived keys are restricted to onboarding-only flows and require a second approval step visible in audit logs.
- Service principals created via SCIM are assigned a default service role (svc-default) and then an automated role-mapping job runs that may assign additional roles based on provisioning attributes. Owner is set to the requestor by default and must be validated in the RBAC console within 14 days.

Redaction guidance we recommend: provide parsed SAML attribute maps (attribute name -> value) + one redacted raw assertion (all SAML:Assertion value attributes with signature/value replaced with "<REDACTED>"). If you need full raw assertions for a small sample we can mark them as restricted and deliver under NDA-specific SFTP path.

We will upload the three files and the README to the HubSpot SFTP target on Wed 18 Jun EOD PT. If you need earlier, tell us which item to prioritize.

— Priyom
Senior Engineer, Access & Provisioning

From: Aisha Clarke <security@medsys.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — service principals & automated provisioning

Nikhil / Priyom — thank you, this looks great. The planned deliverables align with our needs. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Parsed SAML maps + one redacted raw assertion is perfect. We do not need full raw assertions unless there is something unusual.
- For owner emails: first_initial + last_name@<redacted> is acceptable for the scoped dataset; we'll request full emails only if a follow-up audit requires contact verification.
- Can you add a short note in the README about how to reproduce the CSV query (SQL) and any service-account filters used? That helps our auditors replicate.

I'll leave the HubSpot ticket open and will confirm once I see the SFTP drop. Thanks again — Aisha

Aisha Clarke
Sr. Information Security Manager, MedSys Health
security@medsys.com
